get.description: Backs the consent page at `APP_URL/oauth/authorize`, which RFC 8414 metadata advertises as the authorization endpoint. The client pushed its request to the pushed authorization request endpoint first; the page passes on only `client_id` and `request_uri`, and this endpoint describes the pushed request for the signed-in user. Looking it up does not use it up. It never redirects. When the client is invalid, or the pushed request is unknown, expired, already used or another client's (`invalid_request_uri`), the error has no `redirect_uri`: show it to the user. Any other error carries `redirect_uri`, the pushed redirect URI with `error`, `error_description`, the pushed `state` and `iss` (RFC 6749 section 4.1.2.1, RFC 9207); navigate there.

post.description: Records the signed-in user's decision on the pushed request the consent page showed, named by the same `client_id` and `request_uri`. Either decision uses the request up. Approval answers with the pushed redirect URI carrying `code`, the pushed `state` and `iss` (RFC 9207); denial with `error=access_denied`, the pushed `state` and `iss`. The page navigates to `redirect_uri`. Errors follow GET; a request another decision already used answers `invalid_request_uri`.

post.description: Every authorization request is pushed here first. The client authenticates as at the token endpoint and binds the request to its DPoP key (RFC 9449 section 10.1) with a `DPoP` proof header carrying a server-issued nonce, the `dpop_jkt` parameter, or both naming the same key; the authorization code is later bound to that key. A proof is checked as at the token endpoint: `use_dpop_nonce` and `invalid_dpop_proof` answers carry a `DPoP-Nonce` header, and every answer to a verified proof carries the next nonce. Send the browser to the authorization endpoint with only `client_id` and the returned `request_uri`. Baander's first-party client gets `unauthorized_client`. Parameters may be form-encoded (RFC 9126) or JSON. Answers carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.

A missing or invalid proof is answered with `invalid_dpop_proof`, a proof without a fresh nonce with `use_dpop_nonce`; both carry a `DPoP-Nonce` header. Every answer carries the nonce for the next proof and `Cache-Control: no-store`. The issued tokens are bound to the proof key, and to the `X-Baander-Client-Fingerprint` header when it is sent. Parameters may be form-encoded (RFC 6749) or JSON. Every request names its client in `client_id` or in an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header. Public clients authenticate with `client_id` alone; confidential clients add `client_secret`, or `client_assertion` with `client_assertion_type`, by the one method they were registered with. Baander's first-party client gets `unauthorized_client` for every grant; it refreshes at `/api/auth/refresh`. A secret client sends its secret in the body or, with its client ID, in HTTP Basic (`client_secret_basic`, each part form-urlencoded first), never both; a failed Basic authentication is answered with a `WWW-Authenticate: Basic` challenge. A client assertion (RFC 7523 as updated by RFC 10070) is a JWT signed with one of the client's registered keys: `iss` and `sub` are the `client_id`, `aud` is the issuer identifier as its sole value, `exp` and `jti` are required, it lives at most 300 seconds by default, and its `jti` is accepted once. Its `typ` header is `client-authentication+jwt` or absent.

bearerAuth.description: DPoP-bound access token (JWT), sent as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` with a DPoP proof. First-party apps obtain it via `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/login/passkey` or `/api/auth/refresh`; other clients via `/api/oauth/token`. Until the account's email address is verified, its tokens reach only the public routes, `GET /api/auth/me`, `POST /api/auth/email/verify`, `POST /api/auth/me/email/verification`, `PUT /api/auth/me/email` and `POST /api/auth/logout`; every other route answers 403 with `details.reason` `email_unverified`.

oauth2AuthCode.description: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with mandatory S256 PKCE. Token requests need a nonce-bearing DPoP proof, and the issued tokens are DPoP-bound.

scopes.profile: Read the user's own profile (GET /api/auth/me): public ID, name and creation date
scopes.email: Read the user's own profile (GET /api/auth/me) with the email address and its verification date
scopes.library: Browse and stream the user's libraries, control playback on their devices, and use transcoding, favorites, listening history, recommendations and radio
scopes.playlist: Read, create, change, share and delete the user's playlists
